review_notes:
I read all of PrimeIdeals.lean. I also read the simp-relevant declarations it uses in FiniteIntersections.lean: the @[simp] lemmas mem_intersectionSubring_iff and mem_contractedIdeal_iff, the non-simp mem_contractedIdeal_iff_residueMap_eq_zero, the contractedIdeal definition and the IsPrime instance. This file adds no simp attributes of its own.

The file has no rewrite cycles, no competing rules and no unwanted expansion. The main simp normal form is `x ∈ contractedIdeal val i` rewriting to `val i x < 1`, with `mem_intersectionSubring_iff` giving `∀ i, val i x ≤ 1`. The file mostly applies these lemmas explicitly with `.mp` and `.mpr` instead of relying on simp, so I found no simp-interface defect there. The file's `simp [this]` and `simp [hzero]` calls use that normal form directly.

The remaining theorems are iff or classification statements that are used once, namely contractedIdeal_eq_bot_iff, isField_intersectionSubring_iff, isUnit_intersectionSubring_iff and the prime and maximal classifications. Their right-hand sides are existential or disjunctive, and some carry hypotheses. I did not find evidence that marking any of them simp would improve a use. I did not run Lean, so I cannot say whether any simp call is fragile.
